questions.question: 1. Which of the following statements is correct about a binary tree?

answers.a: A node in a binary tree must have exactly two children
answers.b: A node in a binary tree can have at most two children
answers.c: A node in a binary tree can have two or more children
answers.d: A binary tree can have more than one root

explanations.a: Incorrect. A binary tree node may have zero, one, or two children, so having exactly two children is not required.
explanations.b: Correct. A node in a binary tree can have zero, one, or two children, but it cannot have more than two children.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A binary tree restricts each node to a maximum of two children.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A tree is rooted at a single root node, so multiple roots would not describe a single binary tree.

questions.question: 2. Node values in a binary tree always appear in a sorted order from root to leaf, going left to right at each level.

explanations.a: Incorrect. A general binary tree does not require its node values to follow a sorted order.
explanations.b: Correct. A general binary tree has no requirement that node values be sorted. Ordering of values is a property associated with specific tree types such as a binary search tree.

questions.question: 3. Which of the following is TRUE about the leaf nodes of a binary tree?

answers.a: Leaf nodes in a binary tree have no children
answers.b: At least one leaf node in a binary tree has two children
answers.c: Leaf nodes in a binary tree are allowed to have more than two children
answers.d: Leaf nodes in a binary tree may or may not have child nodes

explanations.a: Correct. A leaf node is a node that has no children.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A node with children does not satisfy the definition of a leaf node.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A leaf node has no children, and a binary tree also limits each node to at most two children.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A node that has one or more children is not classified as a leaf node.

questions.question: 4. In a binary tree, all nodes are connected through parent-child relationships.

explanations.a: Correct. A tree is a connected structure in which every node is reachable from the root through parent-child relationships.
explanations.b: Incorrect. If the nodes were separated into disconnected components, the structure would no longer be a single tree.

questions.question: 5. Which of the following is TRUE about a binary tree?

answers.a: There exists a cycle between nodes in a binary tree
answers.b: There may or may not be a cycle in a binary tree
answers.c: A binary tree does not contain any cycles
answers.d: There should be at least one cycle in a binary tree

explanations.a: Incorrect. A cycle violates the defining properties of a tree.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A tree structure is required to be acyclic, so allowing cycles would violate the tree property.
explanations.c: Correct. A binary tree is a tree and therefore does not contain cycles.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The presence of a cycle would make the structure inconsistent with the definition of a tree.

questions.question: 6. Which traversal visits the root node before its left and right subtrees?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Inorder traversal visits the left subtree before the root.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Postorder traversal visits the root after both subtrees.
explanations.c: Correct. Preorder traversal visits the root first, followed by the left and right subtrees.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Level-order traversal visits nodes level by level rather than being defined by a root-left-right recursive order.

questions.question: 7. Which traversal follows the order Left Subtree - Root - Right Subtree?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Preorder traversal visits the root before its subtrees.
explanations.b: Correct. Inorder traversal follows the order Left Subtree - Root - Right Subtree.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Postorder traversal visits the root after both subtrees.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Level-order traversal processes nodes according to their levels rather than this subtree-root-subtree order.

questions.question: 8. A binary tree contains $n$ nodes. How many nodes should a complete traversal visit?

explanations.a: Correct. A complete tree traversal visits every one of the $n$ nodes exactly once.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Omitting one node would mean that the traversal did not visit every node in the tree.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A traversal does not require visiting each node twice.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A traversal of a tree with $n$ nodes does not introduce an additional node.

questions.question: 9. Which statement best distinguishes a binary tree from a binary search tree?

answers.a: A binary tree must store values in sorted order, while a binary search tree does not
answers.b: A binary search tree can have more than two children per node
answers.c: A binary tree cannot be traversed using inorder traversal
answers.d: A binary search tree has an ordering property for node values, while a general binary tree does not

explanations.a: Incorrect. A general binary tree does not require its values to be sorted.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A binary search tree is also a binary tree, so each node has at most two children.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Inorder traversal can be performed on any binary tree.
explanations.d: Correct. A binary search tree imposes an ordering relationship between values in its left and right subtrees, while a general binary tree does not.
